newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-VILLA HALT WIMBLEDON'S WINNING RUN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VILLA HALT WIMBLEDON'S WINNING RUN.

text.p: Wimbledon's 19-match unbeaten run ended with a crushing 5-0 defeat at Aston Villa on Sunday.
Twin strikers Dwight Yorke and Savo Milosevic terrorised Wimbledon with two goals apiece to move on-song Villa into fourth place in the English premier league.
There was little indication of what was to follow in a turgid opening half hour in which neither goalkeeper was tested.
But once Villa broke the deadlock the Dons were simply overwhelmed and Brian Little's side created their own small piece of history.
It was the first time Villa had won five successive matches since the premier league was formed four and a half years ago.
Villa could hardly have wished for a better start to an awesome period in which they also take on Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester United, Newcastle United and Liverpool by mid-January.
The midland side struck twice inside a five-minute spell.
Yorke cashed in on a poor back pass by Kenny Cunningham to give Villa the lead and four minutes later Milosevic raced clear to clip the ball wide of goalkeeper Neil Sullivan.
Villa increased their lead in the 61st minute with a well-crafted third goal when a close-range shot from Milosevic was well saved by Sullivan but Ian Taylor was on hand to head home the rebound.
With 15 minutes remaining Milosevic added the fourth when his shot deflected off a defender and flew into the opposite corner of the net.
The rout of Wimbledon was completed four minutes from time by Yorke, deflecting a low cross from substitute Sasa Curcic into the net for his 11th goal in the last 12 games.
Bookmakers responded to Villa's comprehensive win by halving their title odds to 8-1 from 16-1.
